classification.difficultyReason: Part a is routine: differentiate, factorise, find the first root, then evaluate x and a. Part b sets the hardest demand. The student must separate speed from velocity, find the stationary point of v by differentiating again, and compare |v| at the interior point and both endpoints. The endpoint maximum (15 at t=0) is bigger than the interior extreme (12), so a student who stops at the stationary point gets it wrong. The numbers are integers with no surds, so it is slightly easier than p10-q4, which has similar speed and endpoint comparisons with surds and more parts.

content.prompt: A particle moves along a straight line. Its displacement $x$ metres from the origin after $t$ seconds is given in each part.

children.label: a
children.prompt: $x(t)=t^3-6t^2+9t+2$, where $t\ge0$. Find the displacement and the acceleration of the particle when it first comes to rest.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}v(t)&=3t^2-12t+9\\0&=3(t-1)(t-3)\\t&=1\text{ or }3.\end{align*}$$
The particle first comes to rest at $t=1$.
$$\begin{align*}x(1)&=1-6+9+2=6\\a(t)&=6t-12\\a(1)&=-6.\end{align*}$$
The displacement is $6\ \mathrm{m}$ and the acceleration is $-6\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: $x(t)=t^3-9t^2+15t+4$, where $0\le t\le5$. Find the greatest speed of the particle, and the time at which it occurs.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}v(t)&=3t^2-18t+15\\a(t)&=6t-18\\0&=6t-18\\t&=3.\end{align*}$$
$v''$ is not needed: $a(t)=v'(t)$ changes from negative to positive, so $t=3$ is a minimum of $v$. Compare $v$ at the stationary point and the endpoints:
$$\begin{align*}v(3)&=27-54+15=-12\\v(0)&=15\\v(5)&=75-90+15=0.\end{align*}$$
The speeds are $12$, $15$ and $0\ \mathrm{m/s}$ respectively. The greatest speed is $15\ \mathrm{m/s}$, at $t=0$.
